info.sub_name: 建築・人文・自然對話

description.sub_name: 建築・人文・自然對話
description.describe_ch:
本課程透過建築的視角探討人與自然之間的關係，研究建築環境如何調節人與自然的互動。我們將思考人類在景觀中留下的痕跡、建築在引導感知方面的作用，以及透過全球與生態關係（Bruno Latour、Albena Yaneva 等）的理論框架來重新思考我們在生態系統中的位置。
課程主題涵蓋氣候適應型建築、居住空間以及挑戰以人類為中心設計觀點的後人類視角。本課程強調閱讀相關文獻、撰寫反思報告，並透過小組討論來分析和探討建築專案。
description.describe_eh: This course examines the relationship between people and nature through an architectural lens, exploring how built environments mediate human-nature interactions. We will consider the traces humans leave in landscapes, the role of architecture in directing perception, and theoretical frameworks such as the cosmopolitical (Bruno Latour, Albena Yaneva) to rethink our position within ecological systems. Topics include climate-responsive architecture, lived-in spaces, and post-human perspectives that challenge anthropocentric design. The course emphasises reading relevant literature, writing reflective reports, and the discussion of architectural projects through group discussions.

gradeRuleDescribe.course_pol_en:
I. Classrooms ProtocoL

1.	Diversity and Inclusion .All course activities will be carried out in an atmosphere of friendly participation and interaction among students, respecting and appreciating each student's personal experience, background and perspectives, such as various school systems at home and abroad, diverse enrolment and learning culture s, gender, etc. You are expected to apply the highest academic standards throughout this course and to treat fellow students with dignity and respect.

2.	Expected classroom behavior. Behavior in the classroom should always be prompt, professional, prepared, and courteous. Effective learning can only be achieved by maintaining mutual dignity and mutual respect among classmates, teachers, or other lecturers. In order to ensure a conducive learning environment, everyone is expected to do the following, abide by each other's classroom behaviour rules, and get used to a culture of politeness.

•	Students should attend class on time. If you cannot arrive at the class on time due to your class time, please do not register for the cla ss. Unless you are sick or there is an emergency, you should be in your classroom on time and in your se at before class starts. If you have to leave class early for any reason, please let me know in advance.
•	All students are expected to treat everyone with respect in the classroom and to behave reasonably, responsibly, and courteously at all times.
•	Do not talk, read, sleep or do other non-course-related homework during class, except for group discussions, otherwise marginal conversations should be minimized. If you are sitting next to someone who might be chatting with you during class, move to another seat so you don't give in to temptation.
•	You should listen attentively when classmates present or ask questions. When you present, you should speak loudly to your group or class so that they can hear you clearly.
•	Laptops or tablets are allowed to take notes in class, otherwise they should be put away.
•	Make sure that mobile devices such as mobile phones and PDAs are turned off during class, and put away and keep silent.
•	Students are not allowed to wear earphones in class.
•	Dress neatly without revealing.

3.	It is hoped that the content of the course rules will be described in a professional dialogue mode of the highest standard and mutual respect, with diversity and inclusiveness.
4.	Teachers are able to guide students in ways, what students should do in the learning process, and their due responsibilities.  

II. Course Communication and Netiquette Guidelines  

1. All students shall abide by the following communication regulations:
•	Teaching and learning use o365 mailbox as a common tool for teachers and students to communicate.
•	When communicating with teachers and classmates in emails, bulletin boards, etc., write the information clearly and be polite.
•	Your e-mail must be signed with your name (Chinese + Pinyin)
•	Check the spelling, grammar, and punctuation of the letter.
•	From Monday to Friday, if anyone asks questions about course learning, I will reply to the email within 24 hours. If you just send me information (eg "I will be absent this Friday."), you don’t need to expect an answer.

2. The online classroom is still a classroom. Although classes are taught mostly online, appropriate classroom behaviour must still be observed. Respecting fellow students and teachers is just as important online as it is in the classroom. This course arranges multiple learning tasks to be carried out online in iLearn. You should set aside time to actively participate in online activities and complete all delivered learning tasks. In iLearn, you can interact with your classmates through various online activities and course content to complete course activities.

3.In each online discussion area, do not dominate any discussion strongly, but give other students the opportunity to participate in the discussion, so as to improve the learning experience of everyone in the course.
•	Everyone should keep an open mind and respect the opinion of others
•	Present your ideas appropriately and avoid vulgar or offensive language. Language is easily misunderstood in written communication. If you must emphasise a point, review the statement to make sure no one is offended; then make a statement. Humour and sarcasm can easily be misunderstood, so try to be factual and professional.
•	Write according to the theme, focus and express briefly, and keep it. Online courses require a lot of reading. When writing, keep your sentences to the point and short so that readers don't get lost in lengthy p aragraphs and miss the point of your statement.
•	Read first, then write. Please be sure to read all postings or comments before posting a comment to prevent duplicating comm ents or asking questions that have already been answered.
•	Write a comment text, which should be reviewed and re-reviewed before sending. Sent comments cannot be retracted, so it is important to double check all text to ensure that the intended message is clearly conveyed.
•	The language of network communication. Do not write in all caps and avoid excessive use of emoji, although the use of emoji can help convey non-verbal feeling, excessive use can cause reading difficulties, misinterpretation, such as: (#-.- ),…
•	Avoid using local language or slang, which may lead to misunderstanding.
•	Share tips with other students and don't make fun of someone's reading and dictation skills.
•	Consider the privacy of others. Ask permission before giving out email addresses or other information about classmates.
•	Do not publish inappropriate information. Do not forward virus warnings, chain letters, jokes, etc. to classmates or teachers. Sharing pornographic or insensitive content is prohibited.

III.	Student Responsibilities

1. Before the start of each semester registration, go to the MyFCU personal information form to confirm the basic information you have left in Feng Chia University. Including mobile phone number, email address, correspondence address and other contact information, so that teachers, teaching assistants, or staff of the course offering unit can contact you.

2.Confirm that your Feng Chia University o365 email and NID password are activated. This will be required for identity verification and use of electronic resources, such as online clas srooms, library resources, software resources, access control, online courses, personal learning his tory, MyFCU App and other resources.

3. You should read and understand the syllabus requirements of this course in detail, update the latest information in real time, and manage your study time well.
a.	Check your Feng Chia University email and log in to iLearn at any time to understand the information released by this course.
b.	Abide by integrity, should maintain a high degree of professionalism, actively attend and participat e in the learning commitment of this classroom, and behave with integrity in and out of the classroom.
c.	Use library collections and copyrighted textbooks.
d.	You should fill in the mid-term and final course teaching feedback for this course according to the week and session listed in the teaching progress and content. Your participation and feedback will help me improve my teaching skills, course teaching content and arrangement of activities, and also provide crucial opinions on the teaching quality.
